title: Artificial Turf
prompt: Our client would like us to estimate the market for artificial turf. How would you approach this question?

clarifying_info.answer: Candidate should brainstorm the range of uses before narrowing scope: sports fields (football, soccer, rugby, golf), commercial businesses, residential, airports, and schools (high schools, colleges). The interviewer then prompts the candidate to estimate the number of schools in the US (or another chosen use case).

interviewer_notes: This is a pure market-sizing problem, so rarely is any information provided beyond what the candidate specifically and deliberately asks for. It tests the candidate's comfort with ambiguity. The candidate should lead the discussion, brainstorm the uses of artificial turf, and then be prompted (if needed) to estimate the number of schools in the US as the sizing path.

suggested_framework.summary: Brainstorm the use cases for artificial turf, choose one segment (schools) to size, estimate the number of relevant institutions from US population data, then multiply by turf replaced per year and price per square foot.

stages.interviewer_asks: How would you approach estimating the market for artificial turf?
stages.expected_answer: Candidate brainstorms the range of uses for artificial turf (sports fields — football, soccer, rugby, golf; commercial businesses; residential; airports; schools — high schools and colleges), then proposes narrowing to one use case to size.
good_answer_signals: Generates multiple plausible use cases before calculating anything
Proposes narrowing scope to a tractable segment

stages.interviewer_asks: Let's estimate the number of high schools in the US.
stages.release_when: Only if candidate asks for population data clearly and deliberately
stages.info_to_release: US population 300M; assume ~1% of the population is age 18 (flat age distribution); assume 80% of 18-year-olds attend/attended high school; assume ~250 18-year-olds per high school.
stages.expected_answer: Number of 18-year-olds = 300M × 1% = 3M; attending high school = 3M × 80% = 2.4M; number of high schools = 2.4M / 250 ≈ 9,600.
good_answer_signals: Chains population → attendance rate → class size cleanly

stages.interviewer_asks: Now estimate the number of (bachelor's) colleges in the US.
stages.info_to_release: US population 300M; assume ~1% of the population is age 19; assume 25% of 19-year-olds go to a 4-year college; assume average graduating class size of 400.
stages.expected_answer: Number of 19-year-olds = 300M × 1% = 3M; going to college = 3M × 25% = 750,000; number of colleges = 750,000 / 400 ≈ 1,875.
good_answer_signals: Picks a reasonable average graduating class size

stages.interviewer_asks: And the number of community colleges?
stages.info_to_release: Assume 10% of 19-year-olds go to community college; assume average graduating class size of 200.
stages.expected_answer: Going to community college = 3M × 10% = 300,000; number of community colleges = 300,000 / 200 = 1,500.
good_answer_signals: Applies the same cohort-based method a third time consistently

stages.interviewer_asks: Now put it together — what's the total annual market size for artificial turf in US schools?
stages.info_to_release: Assumptions to use: price of turf = $10/sq ft; turf lifetime = 10 years; athletic field size = 60 yards × 120 yards; adoption rate of turf = 50%.
stages.expected_answer: Total schools = 9,600 + 1,875 + 1,500 = 13,000. Field size = 180 ft × 360 ft = 64,800 sq ft. Annual sq ft of turf bought per school = (1/10 lifetime) × 50% adoption × 64,800 = 3,240 sq ft. Market size = 13,000 schools × 3,240 sq ft × $10/sq ft ≈ $420M.
good_answer_signals: Correctly converts yards to feet before computing area
Correctly amortizes turf purchases over its 10-year lifetime
Arrives at a final market-size figure in the hundreds of millions

stages.interviewer_asks: So, what's your estimate of the market size?
stages.expected_answer: The market for artificial turf in US schools (high schools, colleges, and community colleges) is roughly $420 million per year; candidate should note this covers only the schools segment and that other use cases (sports leagues, commercial, residential, airports) would add further market size if sized separately.
good_answer_signals: Notes the estimate is scoped to schools, not the full addressable market

math.question: How many US high schools are there?
How many community colleges are there?
What is the annual US market size for artificial turf in schools?
steps: Field area = (60×3) ft × (120×3) ft = 180 ft × 360 ft = 64,800 sq ft
Annual sq ft bought per school = (1/10 lifetime) × 50% adoption × 64,800 sq ft = 3,240 sq ft
Market size = 13,000 schools × 3,240 sq ft × $10/sq ft = $421.2M ≈ $420M

synthesis: The annual US market size for artificial turf, sized through the schools segment (high schools, 4-year colleges, and community colleges), is approximately $420 million. This is built bottom-up: ~13,000 total schools, each replacing roughly 3,240 sq ft of turf per year (accounting for a 10-year turf lifetime and ~50% adoption on a 64,800 sq ft field), at $10/sq ft. This figure covers only the schools use case; sizing other uses (professional/amateur sports leagues, commercial, residential, airports) separately would add further market size.
what_great_looks_like: Brainstorms multiple plausible uses for artificial turf before picking one to size
States every assumption explicitly and keeps them internally consistent
Correctly converts yards to feet before computing field area
Correctly amortizes a durable purchase (turf) over its useful life rather than treating it as bought every year at full size
Sanity-checks the final number and is explicit about what it does and doesn't cover
common_pitfalls: Forgets to convert yards to feet (or vice versa) when computing field area
Forgets to amortize turf purchases over the 10-year lifetime, overstating annual demand by 10x
Picks an unreasonable age-cohort percentage or school size without sanity-checking it
Presents the schools-only estimate as if it were the entire addressable market for artificial turf

extraction.notes: Case gives no firm name, only '1st Round'; firm_style_hint reflects that. All book math independently recomputed and matches (market size $421.2M rounds to the book's stated $420M).
